terminology/sentence/824e972c59.text: These terms carry the meanings below throughout.

terminology/sentence/1031118bcc.text: Where a term is also an ordinary English word, the definition here governs.
terminology/sentence/1031118bcc.note: the classes of product every requirement names, defined here

terminology/sentence/996c713eb3.text: **form** — the complete semantic model of one APR document: its version, document type, metadata, section tree, and roles.

terminology/sentence/b05d6ef413.text: A form is ordinary data and carries no cryptographic assertion of its own.

terminology/sentence/96d47806f6.text: **template** — a form whose `documentType` is `template`: the questions, without any particular respondent's answers.

terminology/sentence/507f347ef8.text: **filled form** — a form whose `documentType` is `filledForm`: the questions together with one respondent's answers, naming the template it answers.
terminology/sentence/507f347ef8.note: filler is defined beside it: requirements and tables name the person answering a form (#488)

terminology/sentence/f785121ff6.text: **section** — a named node of the form tree, holding prompts, child sections, or both.

terminology/sentence/870a1936be.text: **prompt** — a single question, owning a label, an optional response, and optional advisory hints.

terminology/sentence/8e6a7c9081.text: **response** — the answer stored for a prompt, always a string.

terminology/sentence/ba4fde65b2.text: **hint** — advisory guidance attached to a prompt, describing how a response might be presented or checked, never whether it is acceptable.

terminology/sentence/c2d5aca3d8.text: **advisory** — never rejecting, altering, or blocking a response.

terminology/sentence/2a5ec99293.text: The opposite of binding, not of important.

terminology/sentence/4a9ed8a8f3.text: **instance** — one repetition of a table section's shape.

terminology/sentence/db4132f585.text: **semantic model** — the information APR defines, independent of how it is written down.

terminology/sentence/8f4a74f0a5.text: Two documents with the same semantic model are the same form.

terminology/sentence/e5114e1a70.text: **source trivia** — everything in the bytes but absent from the semantic model: comments, whitespace, indentation, quoting style, mapping order, and record framing.

terminology/sentence/fd53fa56d0.text: **representation** — a concrete spelling of the semantic model.

terminology/sentence/3108d30bb1.text: APR defines two, APR-JSONC and APR-YAML.

terminology/sentence/dce9320d2b.text: **record** — one complete unit in a stream: either a whole form or one attestation.

terminology/sentence/d8aab592d2.text: **stream** — an ordered transport carrying independent records.

terminology/sentence/61790b85bc.text: **occurrence** — one appearance of a form in a stream.

terminology/sentence/9a41890ae5.text: Two occurrences with identical semantic models remain two occurrences; an occurrence is neither a copy to be collapsed nor a revision of an earlier one.

terminology/sentence/9abe62f176.text: **digest** — the value identifying a semantic model, computed over its canonical serialization rather than over its bytes.

terminology/sentence/f5cc8a4876.text: **manifest** — the list of digests describing a form's parts, holding no plaintext of the values it describes.

terminology/sentence/a5de1058fb.text: **attestation** — an independent record making a cryptographic assertion about a form identified by digest.

terminology/sentence/8be0b4f786.text: **envelope** — an attestation record excluding its own proofs; this is what a proof signs and what a witness references.

terminology/sentence/3ed9a308ba.text: **subject** — the form an attestation asserts about, identified by digest.

terminology/sentence/5afd5b0726.text: **scope** — how much of the subject an attestation covers: the whole document, or a named set of prompts.

terminology/sentence/d5106cdefe.text: **proof** — a verifiable assertion over an envelope.

terminology/sentence/74aaf28021.text: **witness** — a reference from one attestation to the digest of an earlier envelope, recording that its signer saw that assertion.

terminology/sentence/61c756c8b8.text: **profile** — an optional conformance capability an implementation may claim.
terminology/sentence/61c756c8b8.note: reworded without a lowercase obligation word

terminology/sentence/22b71531e4.text: Optional to claim; binding once claimed.

terminology/sentence/2eaaf4dd89.text: **extension member** — a member APR does not define, named with a reverse-DNS prefix by the producer that owns it, carried by a document and preserved across a round trip ([Unknown members](#extensions)).

terminology/sentence/75a1a466d3.text: **non-blank string** — a string containing at least one non-whitespace character.

terminology/sentence/510fe64839.text: A whitespace-only string is treated as absent.

conformance/sentence/c1ee41e38e.text: APR is deliberately layered so that a complete, useful implementation can be written in an afternoon, in any language, on any device.

conformance/sentence/4d8b802c93.note: core is REQUIRED, stated as a row of the profile table; section 3 assigns every section to a profile, and rules on implementations not claiming a profile moved to 3.1 (#486)

profile-core/heading/70a972cc61.note: the heading is a label; the level is in the table

profile-core/sentence/4d0b071201.text: Parse, validate, fill, and write one document in both representations, per [Representations](#representations) through [Text handling](#text-handling).
profile-core/sentence/4d0b071201.note: what core covers, and the conformance clause introducing the profile table; section 3 assigns every section to a profile, and rules on implementations not claiming a profile moved to 3.1 (#486)

profile-core/sentence/ee3726f264.text: A core implementation is fully conformant.

profile-core/sentence/a609705581.text: It is not a degraded one, and it need not emit HTML, PDF, or native controls.

profile-core/sentence/20db25b0f5.text: It exposes the semantic document and its advisory hints for a host application or renderer to use.

profile-streams/heading/ecd71f784f.note: heading label and OPTIONAL row; section 3 assigns every section to a profile, and rules on implementations not claiming a profile moved to 3.1 (#486)

profile-streams/sentence/7db44dcfc4.text: Additionally reads and writes streams of independent records ([Streams](#streams)).

profile-streams/sentence/9d3e6d16b9.text: A core-only implementation given a stream **MUST** report `APR_STREAM_REQUIRES_ITERATION` and **MUST NOT** select a record by position. [APR-CONF-001]
profile-streams/sentence/9d3e6d16b9.note: APR-CONF-001 with a reader as its subject; one refusal behaviour

profile-attestations/heading/08e5864626.note: heading label and OPTIONAL row; section 3 assigns every section to a profile, and rules on implementations not claiming a profile moved to 3.1 (#486)

profile-attestations/sentence/54b72842fc.text: Additionally computes semantic digests and manifests, resolves attestations against forms, looks up witnesses, and reports the verification vocabulary ([Attestations](#attestations)).

profile-attestations/sentence/585de97a07.text: A core-only implementation **MUST NOT** reject a stream containing attestations, and **MUST** preserve attestation records on round-trip. [APR-CONF-002]
profile-attestations/sentence/585de97a07.note: reader duty APR-CONF-002 and writer duty APR-CONF-011

profile-attestations/sentence/4331fa94d5.text: It **MUST NOT** report a document as verified, and **SHOULD** indicate that attestations are present but unchecked.
profile-attestations/sentence/4331fa94d5.note: MUST NOT APR-CONF-005 and SHOULD APR-CONF-012

profile-attestations/sentence/ba9b08879a.text: Saying nothing is better than saying verified; saying "present, unchecked" is better than both. [APR-CONF-005]

profile-attestations/sentence/75b2c33491.text: This profile is optional for a reason of policy, not merely of cost.

profile-attestations/sentence/f89bcc706c.text: **Nobody is obliged to sign, and nobody is obliged to care that something was signed.**

profile-attestations/sentence/37b9d2ac6e.text: A recipient may have every reason to trust a document by other means — they know the sender, they requested the form, the data is low-stakes, or they simply want to read it.

profile-attestations/sentence/6b06b59ed4.text: Requiring verification before data can be used would impose the form author's threat model on every reader, which is not a decision the file format gets to make.

profile-expressions/heading/5b5120ce68.note: heading label and OPTIONAL row; section 3 assigns every section to a profile, and rules on implementations not claiming a profile moved to 3.1 (#486)

profile-expressions/sentence/a7351ab841.text: A core-only implementation **MUST NOT** reject a document that uses expressions and **MUST** preserve the expression strings when writing it back.
profile-expressions/sentence/a7351ab841.note: reader duty APR-CONF-003 and writer duty APR-CONF-013

profile-expressions/sentence/73045fe87c.text: A host rendering the document presents those prompts as ordinary editable fields: a computed field simply becomes a field the user can type into — degraded, but never broken, and never lost. [APR-CONF-003]
profile-expressions/sentence/73045fe87c.note: informative sentence kept; Example 3.4-1 shows APR-CONF-003 and APR-CONF-013; section 3 assigns every section to a profile, and rules on implementations not claiming a profile moved to 3.1 (#486)

declaring-conformance/sentence/270fc876a.text: State the profiles you implement, the submission transports you implement (`https`, `mailto`, both, or none — [Submission targets](#submission)), and the corpus commit you pass.
declaring-conformance/sentence/270fc876a.note: what a claim names, as APR-CONF-014

declaring-conformance/sentence/f3e90ec24.text: "APR 1.0-beta.6 core+streams, submits https, corpus beta6 @ `<sha>`" is a complete and honest claim.
declaring-conformance/sentence/f3e90ec24.note: the format version is now 1.0-beta.7, with 1.0-beta.6 tolerated (#530)

declaring-conformance/sentence/ead2e1956.text: An implementation **MUST NOT** claim a profile without passing the corpus revision it names. [APR-CONF-004]

representations/sentence/3521a28f7b.text: The same form or attestation may be written as APR-JSONC or APR-YAML; comments, whitespace, indentation, scalar spelling, and mapping order have no semantic effect.

model-layers/sentence/11fdba1e01.text: A rule stated at one layer does not constrain another.

model-layers/list-item/d72feea072.text: **Semantic model** — the information APR defines. All APR semantics are properties of this layer.

model-layers/list-item/e382c663e5.text: **Serialization** — the JSON data model the semantic model maps onto: objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null.

model-layers/sentence/599cafb27c.text: Two documents with the same semantic model are the same form, whatever their presentation.

model-layers/sentence/cbc8bbf14d.text: This is what makes a semantic digest ([Digests](#digests)) meaningful: it is computed over the model, never over the bytes.

model-layers/sentence/e46c53e0ef.text: Information is discarded deliberately when moving from presentation to model.

model-layers/sentence/a812f369db.text: Source trivia **MUST NOT** carry APR meaning, and a writer is under no obligation to reproduce it.
model-layers/sentence/a812f369db.note: source trivia is defined in Terminology; that it carries no meaning is a consequence, not a requirement

model-layers/sentence/0efcf6a0dd.text: Everything else — including members APR does not define — **MUST** survive a round trip. [APR-REP-001]
model-layers/sentence/0efcf6a0dd.note: an implementation that reads and writes back is the subject

syntax-conventions/sentence/c7c556d12d.text: APR does not define a grammar of its own.

syntax-conventions/sentence/e76eccf0ca.text: It defines a **delta** against grammars that already exist, so that an implementer reuses a JSON or YAML parser rather than writing an APR one.

syntax-conventions/sentence/2d00757712.text: Grammar in this document is ABNF (RFC 5234).

syntax-conventions/list-item/1e612f39bd.text: **Rules are imported by name.** A rule referenced but not defined here is the rule of that name in the cited specification, unchanged. `value`, `string`, `number`, `member`, and the structural characters are RFC 8259's.

syntax-conventions/list-item/3f85372100.text: **A redefinition replaces the imported rule wherever it appears.** Where this document defines a rule that the cited specification also defines, the definition here governs for APR, and every imported rule that references it picks up the replacement.

syntax-conventions/sentence/e17627c79e.text: Nothing else in the imported grammar changes.

syntax-conventions/sentence/5b0ac24d60.text: A construct this document does not mention is permitted exactly as the cited specification permits it, and one it excludes is excluded wherever it would otherwise appear.

encoding/sentence/50b93af94e.text: A document **MUST** be encoded as UTF-8 (RFC 3629).

encoding/sentence/e0afa210e4.text: A byte-order mark **SHOULD NOT** be written; a reader **SHOULD** tolerate a leading one. [APR-REP-002]
encoding/sentence/e0afa210e4.note: writer omits a byte-order mark (APR-REP-018); reader accepts one (APR-REP-019)

encoding/sentence/769fa60204.text: A reader **MUST** reject ill-formed UTF-8 rather than substituting replacement characters silently. [APR-REP-003]

encoding/sentence/cb2458dfef.text: Every string **MUST NOT** contain U+0000, and **MUST NOT** contain an unpaired surrogate in the range U+D800 to U+DFFF.
encoding/sentence/cb2458dfef.note: one MUST NOT with a string in a document as its subject; meaning unchanged

encoding/sentence/1adb58d6f9.text: Control characters U+0001 through U+001F **MUST NOT** appear, except tab (U+0009), line feed (U+000A), and carriage return (U+000D), which are permitted so that a multiline response can hold the line breaks a person typed. [APR-REP-004]
encoding/sentence/1adb58d6f9.note: the exceptions join the requirement; why they exist is rationale

apr-jsonc/sentence/db62801ed1.text: APR-JSONC is the JSON grammar of RFC 8259 with comments and trailing commas admitted.

apr-jsonc/sentence/c6b87e76b1.text: It is defined as a delta against that grammar, per [Syntax conventions](#syntax-conventions).

apr-jsonc/code/b967a85ff8.text:
```abnf
; Imported unchanged from RFC 8259: value, member, string, number,
; begin-object, end-object, begin-array, end-array,
; name-separator, value-separator, and everything they reference.

apr-jsonc-text  = ws value ws

; REDEFINED. Whitespace admits comments, so a comment is legal
; wherever whitespace is, and nowhere else.
ws              = *( %x20 / %x09 / %x0A / %x0D / comment )

comment         = line-comment / block-comment
line-comment    = %x2F.2F *( %x00-09 / %x0B-10FFFF )
block-comment   = %x2F.2A *( not-star / star-not-slash ) %x2A.2F
not-star        = %x00-29 / %x2B-10FFFF
star-not-slash  = %x2A ( %x00-2E / %x30-10FFFF )

; REDEFINED. A trailing comma is permitted after the final element.
object          = begin-object
                  [ member *( value-separator member ) [ value-separator ] ]
                  end-object
array           = begin-array
                  [ value *( value-separator value ) [ value-separator ] ]
                  end-array
```
apr-jsonc/code/b967a85ff8.note: productions are numbered, and the convention is stated in 4.2

apr-jsonc/sentence/95b00ddd41.text: Because a comment is a production of `ws`, and `ws` never appears inside `string`, **a comment sequence inside a string literal is not a comment.**

apr-jsonc/sentence/ede7985d75.text: The `string` rule is imported unchanged, so `"// not a comment"` is an ordinary string value.

apr-jsonc/sentence/8e7bb536f7.text: This is the first question an implementer asks, and the grammar answers it rather than leaving it to prose.

apr-jsonc/sentence/a1c513d7f0.text: Once comments and trailing commas are removed, the text **MUST** decode as JSON (RFC 8259) to the semantic model.
apr-jsonc/sentence/a1c513d7f0.note: a document matches production [1]; decoding to the model is informative

apr-jsonc/sentence/b95062366c.text: Comments are source trivia and cannot carry APR meaning. [APR-REP-005]
apr-jsonc/sentence/b95062366c.note: comments are source trivia, stated once in the chapter introduction

apr-jsonc/sentence/6c0cdb2458.text: RFC 8259 §4 says object member names SHOULD be unique.
apr-jsonc/sentence/6c0cdb2458.note: RFC 8259's position is described without its keyword

apr-jsonc/sentence/15e687f91b.text: APR raises this: a parser **MUST** reject a duplicate member name rather than applying a last-key-wins rule. [APR-REP-006]
apr-jsonc/sentence/15e687f91b.note: a reader is the subject and the diagnostic is named

apr-jsonc/rationale/9cc307dfbd.text: Rationale: last-key-wins makes a document's meaning depend on which parser reads it, which is precisely what a semantic digest cannot tolerate.

apr-jsonc/sentence/87bcd91af1.text: `scripts/extract-spec-examples.py` derives the conformance vectors from them, so a change to the rule and a change to its evidence are the same edit ([Authority](#scope)).

yaml-resolution/sentence/91f2ad2d85.text: JSON has no representation for it, so there is no value for it to resolve to. [APR-REP-011]

yaml-resolution/sentence/122592194e.text: YAML 1.2.2 chapter 10 presents failsafe, JSON, and core as *recommended* schemas rather than mandatory ones, and a processor may define another.

yaml-resolution/sentence/7255276fb8.text: An implementation therefore uses a YAML library for **syntax** — characters, structure, flow and block style, document streams — and **MUST NOT** use that library's default scalar resolution. [APR-REP-012]

yaml-resolution/rationale/b44dffd624.text: Rationale: this is close to YAML's Core Schema, restricted to what JSON can represent. The narrower JSON Schema is deliberately *not* used: under it a plain scalar that is not a literal has no resolution at all, so `title: Permit Application` would be invalid and every string in an APR-YAML document would have to be quoted. That is not a document anyone would write.  Choosing a YAML 1.2 library instead of a 1.1 one does not remove the need for this table. Under YAML 1.2's Core Schema `012` resolves as the number 12 and `.inf` as a float, so a leading-zero identifier is still corrupted and a non-finite value still appears. The distance being closed here is not between YAML versions; it is between any YAML schema and the JSON value space.

yaml-resolution/sentence/64673256c1.text: Because the target is the JSON value space rather than YAML's, an entire class of YAML-only behaviour disappears without APR enumerating it.

yaml-resolution/sentence/ab1f1b3037.text: Sexagesimals, implicit timestamps, and the YAML 1.1 `y`/`n`/`on`/`off` boolean spellings are not JSON values and therefore resolve as ordinary strings.

json-subset/sentence/1c12df3dc4.text: APR uses a restricted subset of the JSON data model.

json-subset/sentence/1faff29eaa.text: A **response** is always a JSON string ([Responses are strings](#responses)).

json-subset/sentence/448d94d082.text: It is never a number, boolean, array, or object, whatever the prompt's advisory type suggests.

json-subset/sentence/b7b9955dfc.text: Every other member is **structural**: it describes the form rather than carrying what a person typed.

json-subset/sentence/2954a80eba.text: A structural member uses the **JSON type that fits it**, natively: a flag is a JSON boolean, a count is a JSON integer, a numeric bound is a JSON number, and a name, identifier, or piece of text is a JSON string.

json-subset/sentence/e7b56a5a0a.text: A writer **MUST** emit each structural member in the type its member table declares, and a reader **MUST** report a structural member of another type as `WRONG_TYPE` ([Errors](#structural-validation)).
json-subset/sentence/e7b56a5a0a.note: writer emits the declared type (APR-REP-023); reader rejects another (APR-REP-015)

json-subset/sentence/5598c54972.text: `"canAddRows": "true"` is not a boolean and `"maxRows": "25"` is not a count. [APR-REP-015]

json-subset/sentence/f8dae5d803.text: Where JSON has no type for a value, the member is a string in a stated form: timestamps are RFC 3339 strings, and a bound on a temporal field is a string in that field's canonical write form ([Canonical value forms](#canonical-values)).

json-subset/sentence/3659f2887a.text: A structural member is never a string *because* it is structural; it is a string only when a string is the fitting type. [APR-REP-016]

json-subset/rationale/6f2e42e745.text: Rationale: the strings-only rule once applied to the whole document, and the reason for it never did. A response is a string because it carries what a person typed, and typing produces text. A row count does not come from a person; spelling it `"25"` obliges every reader to parse a number out of a string and to decide what `"25.0"` or `" 25"` mean, which is exactly the class of silent divergence the format exists to remove. Native types give the schema the check and give readers nothing to interpret.

json-subset/sentence/cb498e073c.text: A reader tolerates it in a response position only, coercing it to the empty string; anywhere else it is a parse failure. [APR-REP-014]
json-subset/sentence/cb498e073c.note: reader reads a null response as empty (APR-REP-024); reader rejects null elsewhere (APR-REP-014)

responses/sentence/9ef48b65dd.text: A `prompt.response` **MUST** be a JSON string, and a response given as a JSON number or boolean **MUST** be rejected at parse time. [APR-MODEL-001]
responses/sentence/9ef48b65dd.note: a reader is the subject; one MUST

responses/sentence/9965ecc75a.text: It **MUST NOT** be coerced to `"42"` or `"true"`.

responses/sentence/63fd518baf.text: Rejecting and coercing are different failures: one refuses the document, the other accepts it having invented data. [APR-MODEL-049]

responses/rationale/96e1e685bb.text: Rationale: silent coercion is worse than rejection. It produces a document that looks conformant while having invented data that no person entered.

responses/sentence/e08b085ebc.text: A `null` response and an absent `response` member are both read as the empty string.

any-string/heading/0e3e10b240.note: APR-MODEL-127 states the floor that makes "any string" a promise a reader can keep, with the ceiling left to the implementation

any-string/sentence/93858207ea.text: **This is the rule the rest of the format exists to protect.**

any-string/sentence/dd01a64009.text: The format has no opinion about whether that string is "correct". [APR-MODEL-002]

any-string/sentence/db4ccb7c70.text: The distinction is between **document validity** — is this well-formed APR? — and **workflow acceptance** — will the receiving office act on it?

any-string/sentence/4564c36b8b.text: A benefits office may reject a form for a blank field or an unparseable date.

any-string/sentence/f398aa08d2.text: That is a workflow decision, made by a workflow, and it has nothing to do with whether the document is valid APR.

submission/rationale/cf9a5ecc36.text: Rationale: the format defines *where* a completed form may go and borrows *how* from transports that already exist, rather than specifying one. A pre-signed PUT is the industry's common way to accept an upload without handing out credentials, and every S3-compatible store implements it; a `mailto` address is the way an office without any server at all still receives forms. Redirects are refused for the same reason hidden characters are reported: following one delivers the form to a host the author never named. A pre-signed browser POST is deliberately absent — it needs policy fields beyond the URL, which a string entry cannot carry, and every S3-compatible store accepts a pre-signed PUT. No authentication step is defined because a pre-signed URL *is* the authorisation: the grant travels in the query string, so the client never holds a credential.

regarding/rationale/148b131e8f.text: Rationale: a workflow that wants to record something about a form has two bad options and one good one. Editing the form destroys the digest every attestation over it depends on. Widening the form with the receiver's data puts one party's assertions inside another party's document. Writing a new form and naming what it was about leaves every earlier record untouched, and makes each step of a process a document a person can read, a role can own, and a signature can cover — using the primitive the format already has instead of inventing a second one.

generated-ids/sentence/1c46d94bb4.text: A writer **MUST** preserve every valid id it read, and **MUST NOT** invent or replace an id unless the caller explicitly asks it to repair the document; by default a blank id or a duplicate is simply the error [Errors](#structural-validation) says it is. [APR-MODEL-040]

generated-ids/sentence/0164b2b898.text: When asked to repair, a writer generates ids by **content**, so that every implementation repairing the same document arrives at the same names:

generated-ids/list-item/e5afe4116b.text: Take the **title path**: the titles of the enclosing sections from the outermost inward, followed by the member's own `title` (a section) or `label` (a prompt), as a JSON array of strings.

generated-ids/list-item/e228c9cdaf.text: Serialize that array with JCS (RFC 8785), digest it with SHA-256, and encode the digest with base32 (RFC 4648 §6) in lowercase, without padding.

generated-ids/list-item/9eceec4757.text: The id is `s` for a section or `p` for a prompt, followed by the first five characters. `sdwlrh` names the section titled *Applicant*; `pnzapj` names the prompt *Full name* inside it; `sasnpa` names row *Item 1* of a table titled *Expense line items*.

generated-ids/list-item/ae9f5acebc.text: If the result collides with any id already in its namespace, append the member's 1-based position among its siblings to the array and repeat; if it still collides, append its parent's position, and so on outward.

generated-ids/sentence/46fd752094.text: A blank or whitespace-only id receives a generated one.

generated-ids/sentence/7cb44af50c.text: Where two members share an id, **both** are renamed, since neither has a better claim to the name than the other. [APR-MODEL-041]

generated-ids/sentence/c5251286f7.text: Generated ids are short, typeable, and carry no order: two adjacent prompts get unrelated names, and nothing about a name says where it sits.

generated-ids/sentence/7a510f8799.text: A writer **MUST NOT** generate ids that encode position — `q1`, `q2`, `row_3` — because a person reading them will take the sequence to mean something, and inserting one row would then appear to renumber the rest.

generated-ids/sentence/cef2717a5f.text: A renamed id is a changed id, with everything the stability rule above warns of: a `fields` attestation naming the old id resolves to nothing afterwards, which is the honest outcome, since the thing it named is no longer there under that name. [APR-MODEL-042]

generated-ids/rationale/12d1b9573b.text: Rationale: ids are how a filled form is consumed, so a document with a missing or duplicated id is unusable, and *somebody* has to name the member. Deriving the name from what the member is — its label in its place in the outline — means the name is stable for as long as the thing it names is, and means a document repaired on two machines is the same document. Deriving it from a counter would make it stable only by luck and would make the names look like an order. Rows in a table follow the same rule for the same reason: a row's position is already carried by the document order, which is meaningful, and a name that repeats it is a second copy of one fact.

tables/sentence/b36c0612ba.text: Rows are ordinary sections; cells are ordinary prompts.

extensions/sentence/40433a0aa9.text: A reader **MUST** ignore members it does not recognise, at every level, and **MUST NOT** reject a document for carrying them. [APR-MODEL-020]

extensions/sentence/f3480e7f3c.text: A reader **MUST** also **preserve** them: an unrecognised member present on read **MUST** still be present, unchanged, on write. [APR-MODEL-021]

extensions/rationale/0c54f41c15.text: Rationale: without preservation, every additive change to the format is destructive. A document written by a newer version would lose its new members the first time an older reader opened and saved it, silently, with no error anywhere.

extensions/sentence/3c5b3f6244.text: A wrongly-cased member is an unknown member: it is preserved as data, and the property it resembles takes its default.

extensions/sentence/a1c23219a0.text: This is a common source of "my field vanished" reports.

extensions/sentence/e0353c4983.text: **An extension member is named by its owner.**

extensions/sentence/990f531374.text: An extension member name **MUST** begin with a reverse-DNS prefix owned by the producer, followed by a dot: `com.example.priority`, `gov.ct.dmv.routing`.

extensions/sentence/724e684342.text: A reader identifies an extension member by the dot in its name.

extensions/sentence/cb771fb3ea.text: A validator **MAY** report an unrecognised undotted member as `UNPREFIXED_MEMBER`; it **MUST NOT** reject the document, and **MUST** still preserve the member ([Warnings](#warnings)). [APR-MODEL-029]
extensions/sentence/cb771fb3ea.note: the UNPREFIXED_MEMBER row names the warning, APR-MODEL-020 forbids rejecting and APR-MODEL-021 requires preserving an unknown member

extensions/sentence/5e813421a1.text: **An extension member is the author's own data.**

extensions/sentence/fdc7211264.text: It is written by whoever wrote the form, travels inside it, and is covered by its digest.

extensions/sentence/6e056b44a3.text: Data *about* a form written by somebody else — a receipt, a review, a routing decision — is not an extension member: it is a new form naming what it was about ([Related records](#regarding)).

extensions/rationale/e22f6fa32a.text: Rationale: two producers choosing the same member name produce documents that round-trip correctly and mean different things, and a format that cannot add a member without colliding with somebody's private one cannot grow. Reserving the unprefixed space and requiring an owned prefix for everything else closes both problems without a registry, which is what OpenAPI's `x-` and reverse-DNS naming in Java and Apple platforms do. A domain is the one namespace every producer already owns, so no one has to run anything.

roles/heading/efe35aaf43.text: 5.10 Roles — who each part is for

roles/sentence/9057882298.text: Most real forms are filled by more than one person.

roles/sentence/1bef2fb41c.text: A patient completes an intake, a nurse records observations, the office stamps a reference.

roles/sentence/0ce3885302.text: With nowhere to say so, all three arrive as one undifferentiated list and the patient is left guessing which questions are theirs.

roles/sentence/3dc5e28583.text: A section or a prompt **MAY** carry `role`: a short string naming who is meant to fill it in.

roles/sentence/39c434ba61.text: A prompt's role overrides the role of the section containing it, so a single field can be handed back to the patient without splitting the section in two.

roles/sentence/b81dc5dee1.text: The vocabulary is **open**: a reader that does not recognise a role **MUST** present the field normally rather than erroring. [APR-MODEL-025]

roles/sentence/f0d066f1c3.text: A reader with no `name` **MUST** fall back to the identifier, and **MUST** show the identifier rather than erroring where a role is referenced but never declared. [APR-MODEL-050]

roles/sentence/8e5f05caa2.text: Declaring is itself optional and **MUST NOT** be required: a section or prompt **MAY** reference a role the document never declares.
roles/sentence/8e5f05caa2.note: the roles row makes declaring optional, and APR-MODEL-051 forbids rejecting an undeclared role

roles/sentence/2ec71277c3.text: A validator **MAY** warn about an undeclared role; it **MUST NOT** reject one. [APR-MODEL-051]

roles/sentence/4b0ec49481.text: **A role says who a field is for.

roles/sentence/a8e10d87d7.text: It never says who may type into it.**

roles/sentence/d0c0b818e7.text: The format has no identity at fill time — nothing in a document knows who is at the keyboard — so a reader **MUST NOT** refuse input to a field because of its role. [APR-MODEL-027]

roles/sentence/62c6c1b0af.text: What a reader **SHOULD** do is make the answer obvious without being asked.

roles/sentence/8e280f1c3f.text: Where a document declares roles, a reader **SHOULD** let the person say which role they are filling and then show plainly which fields are theirs.

roles/sentence/0fd10e6a84.text: Fields belonging to others stay visible and stay editable; they are marked, not locked.

roles/sentence/6bff7a73e1.text: A reader **SHOULD** also make a role legible to assistive technology, since a visual treatment alone communicates nothing to a screen reader. [APR-MODEL-028]

roles/sentence/62a6ab444b.text: **Accountability comes from attestations, not from the widget.**

roles/sentence/b2c4dba0db.text: A greyed-out box is evidence of nothing: whoever holds the document can edit it directly.

roles/sentence/48fa83cb44.text: A fields-scoped attestation over those prompts, made with the nurse's certificate, is evidence the nurse filled them.

roles/sentence/ef3fe5e76f.text: Roles describe intent; attestations establish fact.

media-types/sentence/78602aba25.text: A filename extension is a **desktop affordance** — it drives icons, file associations, and save dialogs.

media-types/sentence/27f83f4b46.text: It is not part of the data model.

media-types/rationale/8c2db39e04.text: Rationale: a rule letting the extension override `documentType` cannot be implemented anywhere a filename does not exist: an HTTP request body, a database column, a clipboard paste, a mobile share intent, a `postMessage` between frames, a byte array in an enterprise queue. Under such a rule a browser-based reader and a desktop reader would reach *different conclusions about identical bytes* — precisely the interoperability failure the format exists to prevent. A document must mean the same thing everywhere, including where it has no name.

media-types/sentence/f70af2a51c.text: An implementation **SHOULD** write the extension matching `documentType`, and **SHOULD** warn on mismatch rather than silently honouring either one. [APR-SEC-006]
media-types/sentence/f70af2a51c.note: a writer names the file; a reader warns on a mismatch (APR-SEC-015)

media-types/sentence/186a33605f.text: Representation is determined by content, not by name: a reader **MUST NOT** reject a document because its extension disagrees with its content, and **MUST NOT** infer `documentType` from an extension. [APR-SEC-007]
media-types/sentence/186a33605f.note: the clause forbidding documentType from an extension restated APR-SEC-005

media-types/sentence/015bf444a2.text: Converting a template to a filled form is an explicit act: set `documentType` to `filledForm` and record `templateId`.

media-types/sentence/f68d0f7310.text: Implementations **SHOULD** prompt for a new filename so the blank template is not overwritten. [APR-SEC-008]
media-types/sentence/f68d0f7310.note: a host is the subject of APR-SEC-008

media-types/sentence/46a030b43d.text: Where a document travels with a media type, the type names the representation, and the `documentType` member remains authoritative for what the document is.

media-types/table-row/d83af2884c.text: | An APR-YAML document or document stream | `application/vnd.apr+yaml` |

media-types/sentence/da6f9d2625.text: A producer that labels APR content **MUST** use the type above for its representation. [APR-SEC-012]
media-types/sentence/da6f9d2625.note: a writer is the subject of APR-SEC-012

media-types/sentence/28d530a49f.text: A reader **MUST NOT** select APR behaviour from the generic `application/json`, `application/yaml`, or `application/json-seq` types. [APR-SEC-013]

media-types/sentence/bc0a0411fc.text: A reader **MUST NOT** treat a mismatch between a media type and the content as grounds for rejection: the content decides, exactly as for a filename extension. [APR-SEC-014]

media-types/rationale/64ed0045ab.text: Rationale: these three fail independently, and a case citing one bundle could not say which broke. A producer labelling APR-YAML as `application/json` is a mislabelled document; a reader inferring APR from `application/json` treats every JSON file it meets as a form; a reader refusing a mismatch loses a readable document to a header. Only the last is data loss, which is why the content deciding is stated as its own rule.

media-types/sentence/5f99a7052a.text: The types are in the vendor tree of RFC 6838, with the `+json` (RFC 6839), `+yaml` (RFC 9512) and `+json-seq` (RFC 7464) structured syntax suffixes.

media-types/sentence/66c3c88395.text: Registration with IANA by Skeptical Engineering is **pending** ([Open questions](#open-questions)); until it completes the names are a declaration of intent that no other party has claimed.

media-types/rationale/dfa6e4aa45.text: Rationale: a media type is the name a document carries where a filename does not exist — an HTTP body, an attachment, a share sheet. The `+yaml` suffix answers the concern that YAML's own type would mislead a reader: it says YAML syntax and APR meaning, which is the constrained profile APR-YAML is. The `+json` suffix is a mild stretch, since an APR-JSONC document may carry comments; they are representation trivia removed before the text is JSON ([APR-JSONC](#apr-jsonc)). The product-only name `vnd.apr` rather than a vendor-qualified one is deliberate: a media type is never renamed, and the format is meant to outlive its first steward.

warnings/sentence/bb87c499ae.text: Warnings are how an implementation tells a person "this may not be what you meant" without ever telling them "you may not write this."

human-text/sentence/426c522daa.text: Some members exist to be read or heard by a person: `metadata.title`, `description`, `author` and `publisher`; a role's `name` and `description`; a section's `title` and `description`; a prompt's `label`; and the `placeholder`, `helpText` and `suggestedValues` hints.

human-text/sentence/95359cec16.text: Human-facing text **MUST** be in Normalization Form C (UAX #15) and **MUST NOT** contain a code point that is unassigned, a surrogate, private-use, a control other than U+0009 and U+000A, or that UTS #39 classifies with an `Identifier_Type` of `Default_Ignorable`, `Deprecated`, or `Not_Character`.

human-text/sentence/d80430e0d5.note: a validator reports (APR-TEXT-014); presenting and never rewriting are APR-TEXT-013 and 006

human-text/sentence/4cf8fcdb75.text: Beyond that floor, an implementation **SHOULD** apply the confusable and mixed-script detection of UTS #39 to human-facing text and report what it finds, as the authoring-time warning above already asks for titles and labels. [APR-TEXT-012]

human-text/sentence/67b24af9ea.text: **A response is not human-facing text in this sense.**

human-text/sentence/d5d1822764.text: It is what a person typed, and [Filled data — never rewritten](#filled-never-rewritten) governs it: suspicious characters in a response are surfaced and rendered visibly, and the document stays valid.

human-text/rationale/5830eb1175.text: Rationale: the format is meant to be safe for a person to read and to edit by hand, so text addressed to a person must be text a person can see. The Unicode Consortium maintains the list of what is invisible, deprecated, or deceptive; restating it here would put a copy of that list in this document to drift. The rule therefore names the properties and cites the standard that defines them, and the floor is the mechanical part — the part a script can check — while confusable detection, which depends on context and script tables, is recommended rather than required.

expr-language/sentence/2f2ae9f0fd.text: CEL is non-Turing-complete, terminates by construction, and has no I/O or host access, which is why it is safe to evaluate on a document from an untrusted sender.

expr-language/sentence/fb78f73de6.text: The language is **cel-spec release `v0.25.3`**: its language definition, its standard library, and its standard macros.

attestation-scope/rationale/4d04f1c5ea.text: Rationale: a scope covering the response alone fails like this. Sign "No" to *"Have you ever been convicted of a felony?"*, let someone afterwards change the label to *"Do you enjoy long walks?"*, and the signature would still verify — putting a person on record as having answered a question they never saw. Covering the question, its type, and its offered options is what closes that.

attestation-scope/sentence/c7fdb0959e.text: A fields scope is deliberately *not* the whole document: a filler attests to their part, and someone else editing an unrelated section **MUST NOT** be reported as making their attestation `invalid`. [APR-ATTEST-006]

attestation-scope/sentence/cc4547d5a7.text: `subject.digest` names the complete form, so an edit anywhere produces a changed form, and against *that* form the attestation is `unresolved` rather than invalid ([Changed forms](#changed-forms), [Verification vocabulary](#verification)).

attestation-scope/sentence/2a63dc3cb0.text: It stays `valid` against the form it was made over, which is why a workflow retains the original record rather than replacing it.

attestation-scope/sentence/737eaba1bf.text: A verifier **MUST NOT** report `invalid` merely because the form it holds is a later one. [APR-ATTEST-015]

attestation-scope/sentence/f21abc19f7.text: A verifier **MAY** additionally compare a `fields` manifest's entries against a changed form and report which attested paths still match.

attestation-scope/sentence/72adb1e5b7.text: That is a diagnostic and **MUST NOT** be reported as a verification result: the attestation remains an assertion about its original subject and is never transferred to another. [APR-ATTEST-016]
attestation-scope/sentence/72adb1e5b7.note: the prohibition is APR-ATTEST-032 (#445); that nothing transfers is APR-ATTEST-009

attestation-scope/rationale/b32e2ac9b1.text: Rationale: the promise above is worth making and was worth stating precisely. Read loosely it suggests a fields attestation keeps verifying across edits, which nothing in the format delivers, because a digest over the whole form moves when any part of it does. What the format does deliver is that a filler is never reported as having signed something false — and, for a reader that wants it, a per-path answer to what actually changed.

proofs/sentence/926542560d.text: `proofs` are assertions over the JCS serialization of the attestation envelope after omitting `proofs` themselves.
proofs/sentence/926542560d.note: the signing input is APR-ATTEST-035 and 036 (#452)

proofs/sentence/72f189b7ac.text: This specification defines one proof type, `cms/ecdsa-p256-sha256`: ECDSA over the P-256 curve with SHA-256 (FIPS 186-5), carried as CMS SignedData (RFC 5652), encoded as base64 (RFC 4648), with the X.509 certificate chain (RFC 5280) included.

proofs/sentence/19c3bbac76.text: A proof **MUST NOT** invent a second copy of the subject digest or scope. [APR-ATTEST-007]

proofs/rationale/3659461b92.text: Rationale: two copies of one fact is a correctness bug everywhere in this format, and here it is a security hole: a verifier that checks a second copy reports a signature valid after the real value has changed.

proofs/sentence/7767a27bcb.text: A verifier that does not recognize a proof type **MUST** report it as **unverifiable**, never as invalid, and **MUST** preserve it.

proofs/sentence/8a4c9ba73f.text: "I cannot check this" and "this is forged" are different statements and **MUST NOT** be conflated in a user interface. [APR-ATTEST-008]
proofs/sentence/8a4c9ba73f.note: a renderer is the subject: APR-ATTEST-039

proofs/sentence/9f816a18dc.text: **A proof MAY carry a claimed signing time.**

proofs/sentence/fcc697f68f.text: In `cms/ecdsa-p256-sha256` that is the CMS signing-time signed attribute (RFC 5652), which sits inside the signature and therefore cannot be altered without breaking it.

proofs/sentence/85c3890f64.text: What nothing vouches for is the clock: the value is the signer's assertion that they signed then, and no more.

proofs/sentence/951fd06078.text: A reader that shows it **MUST** show it as claimed rather than proven, and **MUST NOT** derive from it that one record precedes another. [APR-ATTEST-014]

proofs/rationale/36adab67e2.text: Rationale: every signature format works this way, and pretending otherwise is how a plausible timestamp becomes evidence it was never entitled to be. Trusted time needs a time authority, which this baseline does not define. A claimed time is still worth carrying, because it is what the signer said.
proofs/rationale/36adab67e2.note: a time authority this specification does not define

witnesses/sentence/cedfe5ed4f.text: `witnesses` is an ordered, duplicate-free list of semantic digests of earlier attestation envelopes, again excluding `proofs`.
witnesses/sentence/cedfe5ed4f.note: APR-ATTEST-042 and 043 (#452); nothing defined an order, so the word is gone

witnesses/sentence/bf7d84255e.text: It records that this attestation's signer explicitly witnessed those assertions.

witnesses/sentence/ff28f7bfac.text: Witnessing neither authorizes a change nor proves a clock order, workflow acceptance, real-world identity, or trusted time.

changed-forms/sentence/707fb5b174.text: A changed form is another complete form occurrence with a different subject digest.

changed-forms/sentence/3e2a9e8a9b.text: Earlier attestations remain assertions about their original subject and **MUST NOT** be transferred to the changed form. [APR-ATTEST-009]

changed-forms/sentence/e4ce1e77ac.text: Multiple attestations may target one unchanged form, and an attestation may be encountered before its subject.
changed-forms/sentence/e4ce1e77ac.note: a reader is the subject: APR-ATTEST-044 and 045 (#452)

changed-forms/sentence/99734e4b75.text: **Say what happened, not only what is missing.**

changed-forms/sentence/a161d8e665.text: An attestation whose subject resolves to nothing is `unresolved` ([Verification vocabulary](#verification)), and that is the whole of what the vocabulary states.

changed-forms/sentence/0fc1ebf64c.text: Where a verifier holds a form occurrence that is not the subject, it **SHOULD** report both facts: that the attested form is absent, and that a different form is present. [APR-ATTEST-020]

changed-forms/rationale/019e85e89e.text: Rationale: the common cause of an unresolved attestation is not a lost file. It is that somebody opened the form, corrected a typo and saved. Reporting only that the signed document is missing is true and sends that person looking for a file that was never lost, when what they need to know is that the one in front of them is no longer the one that was signed. The result stays `unresolved`, because the assertion really does have no subject here; what this adds is the second fact beside it.

changed-forms/rationale/adc69ba730.text: Rationale: this is how a workflow builds revision history without APR defining one. A sequence of forms with attestations that witness each other is a chain whose relationships are proved. A sequence of forms without them is just several forms, and the format declines to guess.

verification/table-header/d5d09ca4e5.note: the vocabulary carries Condition, Requirement and Rule columns

verification/table-row/c7aecfd9fa.text: | `valid` | The subject resolved, digest and manifest match, and a recognized proof verifies. |

verification/table-row/9a7085f3a5.text: | `invalid` | A recognized proof fails, or a resolved subject differs from the attested digest or manifest. |

verification/table-row/339d6f01dd.text: | `unresolved` | No matching form occurrence is available. |

verification/table-row/2ad5dc341e.text: | `unverifiable` | Required representation, extension, digest, or proof support is unavailable. |

verification/table-row/fe81317660.text: | `witnessed` | One or more referenced envelopes resolve and match. |

verification/sentence/4ae1606faa.text: These are independent, and a verifier **MUST** report them independently: an attestation may be both `unverifiable` and `witnessed`, and `unresolved` **MUST NOT** be reported as a failure of the assertion. [APR-ATTEST-018]
verification/sentence/4ae1606faa.note: not reporting unresolved as a failure is APR-ATTEST-051 (#445)

verification/sentence/71d63c0580.text: A self-signed certificate can produce a perfectly valid proof that proves nothing about identity.

verification/rationale/b155504cb3.text: Rationale: collapsing content validity and certificate trust into one green checkmark teaches people to trust a checkmark that does not mean what they think.

never-gate/sentence/bd0b22288b.text: **An attestation is an assertion about a document, never a permission to read it.**

never-gate/sentence/7a71fc407a.text: An implementation **MUST NOT** treat the presence, absence, or state of an attestation as authorization to read, or to withhold, the data a form carries. [APR-ATTEST-019]

never-gate/sentence/c282b8b588.text: A form with no attestation is a complete, ordinary, fully valid APR document.

never-gate/sentence/1991cb6428.text: An implementation **MUST NOT** require one in order to save, send, accept, or process a form, and **MUST NOT** present an unattested document as deficient. [APR-ATTEST-011]
never-gate/sentence/1991cb6428.note: a renderer presenting a form as deficient is APR-ATTEST-052 (#445)

never-gate/sentence/3ca6b52842.text: **Acting on an attestation is never required.**

never-gate/sentence/24dafdbc5f.text: An implementation **MUST NOT** refuse to parse, validate, render, print, export, or extract data from a document because its attestations are absent, unrecognized, expired, untrusted, or outright invalid.

never-gate/sentence/ebec3809fc.text: Attestation state **MUST NOT** appear in the validation error list. [APR-ATTEST-012]
never-gate/sentence/ebec3809fc.note: a validator is the subject: APR-ATTEST-053 (#445)

never-gate/sentence/18ac6cd9b9.text: An implementation **MAY** warn, badge, or refuse to *act* on a document by its own policy — a receiving workflow is entitled to reject an unattested permit application.
never-gate/sentence/18ac6cd9b9.note: the rule ID moved onto the permission; reworded so an ordinary English word is not read as a class of product (#488)

never-gate/sentence/6ae15f04e8.text: It is not the file format's, and a reader that enforces it on the workflow's behalf has taken a choice away from every other consumer of the same document. [APR-ATTEST-013]

never-gate/rationale/a3ba24e973.text: Rationale: the reasoning is the same one behind [Any string is a valid response](#any-string). A format that withheld data until a cryptographic condition was met would fail exactly when it is most needed: an expired certificate, a verifier that does not recognize a proof type, a proxy that re-encoded the bytes, an archived form whose signing authority no longer exists. In every one of those cases the answers a person wrote are still there, still true, and still the reason the document exists. **The data outlives the attestation, and the format must let it.**

renderers/sentence/acec53c8b9.text: A renderer decides everything, and a GUI, web page, terminal, voice system, and API client are equally legitimate.

primitives/sentence/dcb3bfdb15.text: **A concept earns a primitive when its content cannot be posed as questions and answers, and when a reader computes over it rather than rendering it.**

primitives/sentence/d0e2c2ffd3.text: The two halves are one distinction seen from either side.

primitives/sentence/11a63af508.text: An attestation earns its record kind on both counts.

primitives/sentence/bce8df1b2c.text: Nobody types a digest, so there is no question to ask and no label to render, and its correctness is settled by computation — a mode this format refuses for responses ([Any string is a valid response](#any-string)).

primitives/sentence/63d96a63dd.text: Nothing about it would fit inside a form either: a manifest is nested computed structure, and a response is always a string a person typed ([Responses are strings](#responses)).

primitives/sentence/98ce9e7a58.text: A table does not, and [Tables](#tables) says so directly.

primitives/sentence/ff09dcf039.text: Rows are ordinary sections and cells are ordinary prompts, and carrying `kind` is a claim about structure that already exists rather than a new thing.

primitives/sentence/a757ef1211.text: Tables are as common as anything proposed since, and commonness is not the test.
primitives/sentence/a757ef1211.note: compared tables with later proposals; commonness is the point

primitives/sentence/d4816d8e3c.text: What it holds — when something arrived, under what reference, by what route — is answers with labels, read by people.

primitives/sentence/0aca58c2ab.text: It is a form an office fills in, and [Related records](#regarding) is how it names what it was about.

primitives/sentence/4c948d386d.text: The separate claim that the bytes received are the bytes sent is an attestation made by the receiver, which needs nothing new either.

primitives/sentence/a8ddec5988.text: The failure this test prevents is a format that grows a document kind for every common step of every process.

primitives/sentence/5796a4537f.text: Fixing what a receipt contains would mean modelling one jurisdiction's intake — the mistake [Hints](#hints-object) already refuses at the field level when it declines country-specific types.

primitives/sentence/73635d525b.text: A vocabulary of published templates carries that weight one layer up, where two offices disagreeing costs nobody else anything.
